title: Provider success evidence must contain a nonempty schema and positive rows
context: The existing provider evidence validator treated interface.status=success as sufficient even when fields was empty or row_count was zero. That could allow an empty provider response to participate in provider-side readiness if the surrounding attestation claimed real data and all market boundaries were verified.
decision: A successful interface record must contain at least one nonempty field name.
A successful interface record must have row_count greater than zero.
Failed real interface attempts may still record an empty field list and zero rows and remain fail-closed.
This gate does not contact a provider, does not use credentials, does not create real provider evidence, and does not authorize opening frozen holdout data.
rationale: Provider-side readiness is evidence about a real usable response, not merely a claimed status string. Empty successful responses are insufficient evidence and must fail closed.
